newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close mixed in muted session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close mixed in muted session.

text.p: Argentine stocks clawed back most losses to end mixed Monday in slack trading, with volume drained by the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.
But traders said the market was firm and could be ready to move back to the upside.
"We continued Friday's downward correction today, but cash flows were very tight with scant selling which means the market is soaking up profit-taking," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index closed flat at 584.03, pulling off a session low of 580.61.

"We were helped by the Dow's record close above the key psychological 6,000 level, which seems to augur a strong second-half in October on Wall Street with a prevailing cheerful mood ahead of the (U.S.) elections," said Alessandro.
The MerVal closed up 1.2 percent last week at 584.32, recording its seventh consecutive week of gains on the back of government austerity reforms and improving economic indicators.
Traders said steady buying by the private pension funds (AFJPs) was underpinning the bolsa.

"The AFJPs are building up their positions in stocks, which is offsetting the market's mild correction," said Miguel Daneri of Boston Securities. "If U.S. long bond yields stay at present levels after today's holiday, then the bolsa should be able to regroup and quickly head back up."
In the session floor volume shrank to 7.4 million pesos from an also very weak 11.6 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to a negligible tally of 17 million pesos.
The broad market index shed 0.2 percent, with losers edging out risers 21 to 19 and 16 issues closing flat.
Best main-tier performers were petrochemical concern Indupa, carmaker Ciadea and Banco de Galicia, which advanced 1.9 percent, 1.7 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by petrochemical company Ipako, which slid 2.2 percent, carmaker Sevel, off 1.9 percent, and sugar refiner Ledesma, down 1.6 percent.
